summary: Four high-severity findings: the unrestricted positive-characteristic symmetric-power polarization is false; the non-ordinary inertia formula has the wrong sign for the extraction's normalization; the full local comparison and its crystalline component omit an unramified quadratic twist, visible at p=79; and the polarized-lifting brief imports a downstream ML.5 while supplying ML.2/ML.3. The main existence theorems are not refuted. Existing E1-E8 are distinguished from these defects, and the report provides exact matrix and graph regressions.

Downloaded pages outside these ranges are not counted as read. The report records URLs, hashes and limitations.

Checked the arXiv submission history (v3 remains the latest listed version), Calegari's research listing and web searches for a correction. No correction of the two local formulas was found in those checks; this is not an exhaustive claim about correspondence or unpublished corrections.

Read the upstream ClassicalGroups and ReductiveGroups roadmaps, and the relevant ModularForms Layer 4 contract. Characteristic-zero classical representation theory is not a supplier for an unrestricted modular symmetric-power self-duality theorem. No upstream roadmap is replanned here.

This concerns a proposed brief, not an assertion that the current base graph is cyclic.

Exact finite-field elimination for SL2(F7) on Sym^d for d=5,6,7 gives one-dimensional spaces of invariant bilinear forms, with nonzero ranks 6,7,6 respectively. Frobenius trace regressions at p=7,11,13,79,107 distinguish the untwisted and corrected local comparisons. Inertial exponent multisets remain equal for all m<3(p+1) coprime to p+1 at p=7,11,13,79: that test alone cannot detect the unramified error.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25.result.json: symmetric-power-polarization; route 3 to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7; corresponding reader explanation
findings.claim: The item asserts a nondegenerate polarization of Sym^(n-1) of any two-dimensional representation over F without a characteristic or degree restriction. This is false in positive characteristic, even when the original representation is symplectic and the characteristic exceeds 5. A possibly degenerate invariant form does not make the representation GSp- or GO-valued.
findings.evidence: Take F=F7, Gamma=SL2(F7), its standard two-dimensional representation and n=8. On v_i=x^(7-i)y^i, solve U^t B U=B and L^t B L=B for the elementary generators U:x->x,y->x+y and L:x->x+y,y->y. Exact elimination of the 128 linear equations in 64 variables gives a one-dimensional invariant-form space. A generator has B(v_i,v_(7-i))=-i for 1<=i<=6 and all other entries zero. Every nonzero form has rank 6, with radical span{x^7,y^7}; none is nondegenerate, even after scalar extension. The report includes the executable calculation. The published paper only applies this construction at p>5 and n=p-2,p-1,p (pp. 513 and 516), where (n-1)! is invertible. Tau Ceti's pinned Representation.symmetricPower constructs the representation in arbitrary characteristic and proves no unrestricted nondegenerate pairing theorem.
findings.fix: State the pairing theorem in the actual range: characteristic zero, or odd characteristic p with 1<=n<=p; alternatively give the precise factorial-invertibility and 2-invertibility hypotheses. Specify and prove nondegeneracy of the induced form, its symmetry sign and multiplier, and the basis/form identification used for G_n. Keep the existing symmetric-power functor and G7 ownership. Test degrees p-2 and p-1 positively and degree p negatively. This is an overgeneralization by the extraction, not a new error in the paper.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25.result.json: nonordinary-local-shape, lubin-tate-characters, large-image-nonordinary note and local-shape-theorem-3-1 note; corresponding reader and sourceIssues
findings.claim: The positive inertia exponents in nonordinary-local-shape contradict the fixed cohomological normalization det(rho_f)=epsilon^(1-k). The later definition of omega_2 as the reduction of the Lubin-Tate character, and the negative exponent in rho_n_m, prevent treating this as an unspecified choice of convention.
findings.evidence: The item claims rho-bar_f|I_p = omega_2^(k-1) + omega_2^(p(k-1)), whose determinant is epsilon-bar^(k-1), since omega_2^(p+1)=epsilon-bar|I_p. The representation-of-eigenform item and published pp. 512-513 fix determinant epsilon^(1-k). At the actual p=79,k=38 instance, the two determinant exponents modulo 78 are 37 and 41. Pepin-Schmidt, Irreducible mod p Lubin-Tate (phi,Gamma)-modules, author copy 26 November 2019, section 2 pp. 2-3, gives the fundamental-character norm identity and identifies the fundamental character with reduction of the Lubin-Tate character. Images of published p. 516 and arXiv v3 p. 8 confirm that the positive signs are in the source, not OCR artifacts. None of E1-E8 records this mismatch.
findings.fix: With the existing epsilon_2 and cohomological conventions, replace both exponents by 1-k and p(1-k). Update the dependent local-shape and dihedral-check explanations while retaining the unchanged projective order and gcd conclusions. Record the printed sign mismatch as a source issue with its checked versions and determinant regression. If instead choosing a dual fundamental-character convention, change every Lubin-Tate, induction and Hodge-Tate formula consistently; do not leave the sign discretionary in one note. The separate unramified correction in /3 is still required.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25.result.json: local-shape-theorem-3-1, deformation-ring-nonordinary, route 1 local/deformation brief; corresponding reader and sourceIssues
findings.claim: The asserted full G_Qp-isomorphism Sym^(p-1)(rho-bar_f) = rho-bar_(p,1) drops an unramified quadratic twist when p=3 mod 4. The note incorrectly says the two-dimensional normalization differs only by an unramified quadratic character. Consequently rho_(p,1), as defined using a Lubin-Tate character trivial on the uniformizer, is not a lift of the specified residual representation at p=79 and cannot label its local deformation component.
findings.evidence: Choose a Frobenius lift phi corresponding to the uniformizer, so epsilon-bar(phi)=1 and epsilon_2(phi^2)=1. Ordinary induction Ind epsilon_2^(-m) has Frobenius matrix S=[0,1;1,0], determinant -1. An irreducible rho-bar_f with the prescribed determinant and the same two inertia characters has Frobenius matrix conjugate to A=[0,-1;1,0], determinant +1. Matching them requires an unramified lambda with lambda(phi)^2=-1, not lambda^2=1. On Sym^(p-1), traces are respectively 1 and (-1)^((p-1)/2), from the unique fixed middle monomial. At p=79 these are 1 and 78 in F79, hence the representations are not isomorphic. Pepin-Schmidt section 2 p. 2 explicitly distinguishes ordinary induction from determinant-normalized induction by exactly this character. Published p. 517 and arXiv v3 p. 9 assert the untwisted isomorphism and use its lift for R; their preceding definition fixes epsilon_2(Art(p))=1. The extraction's successful inertia-multiset test cannot see an unramified character.
findings.fix: Let eta be the unramified quadratic character of G_Qp. After the sign correction of /2, use rho-bar|G_Qp = eta^((p-1)/2) tensor rho-bar_(p,1), and choose eta^((p-1)/2) tensor rho_(p,1) as the local crystalline lift and component label. State the determinant-normalized two-dimensional induction with lambda(phi)^2=-1. The twist has weight zero and square 1, preserving the GO_p multiplier epsilon^(1-p). Track it through the tensor step: it becomes trivial on G_Fv because F_v contains Q_(p^2), so the paper's displayed identities there remain available. Record this additional source error and the p=79 Frobenius regression. This repairs the local proof input; it does not change or refute the main global existence theorem.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25.result.json: route 2, PolarizedAutomorphyLifting brief/reason; corresponding reader route explanation
findings.claim: The proposed polarized-lifting roadmap imports cyclic base change and automorphic induction from the whole of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.5 while explicitly supplying ML.2 and ML.3. With the registered dependencies this closes a cycle. Naming a Part II does not make that downstream stage an available input.
findings.evidence: Route 2 says ML.2 and ML.3 consume the proposed lifting theory, and names ML.5 among its imports. The assembled stage graph has ML.2 -> ML.3 -> ML.5, with ML.5 also requiring ML.4. Thus ML.3 -> ML.5 -> PolarizedAutomorphyLifting -> ML.3 is a cycle. A graphlib check reproduces it by adding only the brief's relationships to the otherwise acyclic 2907-stage graph. Related early-base-change defects were already reported in RT-AREA-langlands-1/1 (confirmed) and RT-PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/6 (report; no review file present here); the present finding identifies this extraction's still-unrepaired brief, rather than claiming the general ownership problem was previously unknown.
findings.fix: Have route 2 consume an explicitly early, source-scoped base-change/automorphic-induction interface, coordinated with the existing EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison early-transfer repair and GL2 specializations. Keep generic transfers owned once and ML.5 as their downstream registration/endpoint consumer. State the early interface's prerequisites and the handoff to the eventual design/blueprint rather than assuming an unregistered prefix exists. Recheck the expanded graph including the proposed supplier and its ML.2/ML.3 consumers. Update only this extraction and its design instructions in the resulting fix; base-stage edits belong to their authorized blueprint/fix jobs.
